source.display_title: 05/04/2026 - Andrew Freeman x Farooq Bey  — Closed

prospect.name: Andrew Freeman
prospect.occupation: Physician assistant (PA). Currently in what he describes as a difficult job situation where he has struggled to stand up for himself. Wants to move toward coaching men and building or joining a faith-based ministry.
prospect.family_status: Engaged — hoping to marry in June 2027, date not yet set. The relationship broke down about a year ago and was repaired. Wants children.
prospect.training_background: Former college tennis player, lifelong athlete, plays a lot of pickleball. Has stopped playing tennis because of the knee injuries. Has worked with a personal trainer for the last few years on a full-body programme focused on breathing and on keeping muscle long and flexible rather than shortened, which requires substantial equipment. Has consistently avoided traditional weightlifting on advice.
prospect.medical: Scoliosis, disclosed in the first ninety seconds. Has always been advised against traditional weightlifting because of it — 'I've always been told not to lift heavy weights... because I have scoliosis, and my back's always been a huge issue.' Chronic daily back symptoms — 'my back just kills me at the end of the day' — which he later qualified as stiffness, ache and discomfort rather than acute pain. Asymmetric back musculature which he attributes to scoliosis plus a tennis career. Injured both knees, has completed a course of physical therapy and considers them roughly back to baseline but still needs strengthening. Mental health: diagnosed-in-effect anxious attachment, chronic anxiety, and a self-described chronic fight-or-flight state affecting attention and prioritisation; family dysfunction growing up; has been in coaching for it. No clinician was consulted, named or contacted on this call and no clearance was sought.

signals: The defining constraint is present and explicit — a standing instruction against loaded lifting: 'I've always been told not to lift heavy weights, like not to do traditional weightlifting, because I have scoliosis'
Textbook high intent with no price resistance: scored the offer 9 or 10, said 'the financial investment, yeah, it's a concern, but it's not going to stop me', and chose the top $9,000 tier unprompted

IMPORTANT DEVIATION FROM THE ARCHETYPE: this avatar normally describes someone the programme loses to a clinical block. Here the block was not honoured — the rep answered it with 'it's not an issue' and a near-promise to remove 99.9% of his discomfort — and the deal closed. This is the same profile as the Tyron Giuliani case inverted, and is the more consequential version of it.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED: the_rebuilder also fits — a former college athlete who stopped playing after injuring both knees, wants to play sports again, and carries visible regret about a hard few years. Assigned as medically_constrained because the clinical constraint, not the lost former self, is the fact that decides this call.

goals.text: Feel strong and able to actually lift and do things with his body — functional strength rather than gym numbers
Be strong but still flexible and unrestricted, so he can play sports and move the way he wants
Resolve the back issues — 'my back feels great, I don't have any back issues'
Build discipline through accountability, which he says is the thing he has never been taught
Improve mental health and reduce anxiety, which he has already seen improve when training is consistent
Be present and physically capable for his future wife and children, and be around and not in pain for them
Show up on the aisle at his wedding confident, powerful and full of life — 'thriving for once'
Build the confidence to lead others, coach men, and move into ministry
Look back in a year and be proud that he had courage and did not give up

pains.text: Scoliosis with chronic daily back stiffness and ache that worsens through the working day
Bilateral knee injuries that ended his tennis and required a completed course of physical therapy
Has been shut out of strength training entirely by standing advice not to lift, and has therefore never built a base
Chronic anxiety and a fight-or-flight state that crowds out his own priorities — 'I sacrifice the priorities of taking care of myself so that I can appease other areas of my life'
Anxious attachment traced to family dysfunction, which cost him the relationship for a period — 'she broke up with me a year ago because of this'
Lack of confidence and a belief that he brings no value — 'just feeling like there's something wrong with me'
Never taught internal discipline — 'my dad didn't teach me that, he taught me a different way of just do this or else'
Has repeatedly failed to stay consistent with training on his own
A difficult and unstable work situation in which he has struggled to advocate for himself
Poor posture he actively works on
Existing trainer's programme requires a lot of equipment, making it hard to sustain

objections.raw_quote: I've always been told not to lift heavy weights, like not to do traditional weightlifting, because I have scoliosis, and my back's always been a huge issue.
objections.rep_response: Offered a staff testimonial — a UK colleague named Harry who has scoliosis and 'before he could barely touch his knees, now he's able to touch his toes' — and asserted that this way of training 'returns your body to the way it's designed to operate'

objections.raw_quote: And so with scoliosis, even that shouldn't be an issue?
objections.rep_response: Said x-rays may be requested, that otherwise 'we can work around it. But it's not an issue', and then near-promised the outcome: 'what I can nearly promise you is that we're going to remove at least 99.9% of the discomfort or pain that you're going through'

objections.raw_quote: the investment, because I don't really know where it is monetarily, it's like that does, that's definitely a concern just because of this work situation I'm going through, but I'm still very ready to do this, and I don't think it would really impact my decision.
objections.rep_response: Did not explore it. Answered 'And I hold you accountable to that, yeah?' and moved to the pillars

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, it's going to be tighter financially, but I have it, so yeah.
objections.rep_response: 'Good. I don't want you to be broke. I don't want to take food off your table. But I want it to be a bit uncomfortable.'

objections.raw_quote: I have a unique phone... It's called the Wise Phone. It doesn't have any internet connection. You can only download, it has apps, but it allows certain apps to be downloaded, ones that aren't addicting.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed desktop and laptop access is available without checking which platform components are desktop-capable

offer.payment_plan_terms: Referenced only in passing — 'Most people put on a credit card, Andrew, but as I said, there's different ways we can kind of structure it.' No plan was built and none was needed; the prospect took the twelve-month tier.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Not a guarantee in commercial terms but a clinical one: 'I'm not going to make your spine like this, but what I can nearly promise you is that we're going to remove at least 99.9% of the discomfort or pain that you're going through.' Also 'The byproduct of that is alleviating all of the back pain that you've mentioned to me on the call.'

evidence: Selected the top tier himself when asked: 'Is it the 12 that you're leaning towards?' — 'I think so... Yeah, it's going to be tighter financially, but I have it, so yeah.'
Explicit agreement: 'Ready to rock and roll?' — 'Yep, I am.' — 'Let's do it, my friend.' — 'Let's do it.'
Payment collection was initiated on the call: 'Okay, so I'll just get the link up for you' followed by confirmation of his email address letter by letter
Commitment was obtained before price, cleanly: 9 or 10 on the trust gauge, 'I'm all in', and 'do you personally feel internally capable of making that happen?' — 'With help. Yes. Definitely.'

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: no payment confirmation is observable. The recording ends at 'What I'm going to do, obviously, sensitive information. I'll take my recorder out of this call' — the same pattern as the Shazad Irani close on 05/01.
COUNTER-EVIDENCE: he disclosed real financial uncertainty tied to an unstable job twelve minutes before committing $9,000, and the rep never established capacity.
outcome.next_step: Rep to process the $9,000 twelve-month investment, grant access to the app and community, and book the one-to-one call with Trevor

notable.note: The highest-risk call in this batch by a wide margin, and it closed at the top tier. A 31-year-old with scoliosis, a standing instruction from others never to lift, chronic daily back symptoms and two recently rehabilitated knees was sold a loaded ballistic kettlebell programme in 33 minutes. No health question was asked; every clinical fact came from the prospect volunteering it. The rep answered the scoliosis concern with an employee testimonial and the words 'it's not an issue', then near-promised removal of 99.9% of his discomfort. No clinician was named, contacted or suggested at any point. Separately and independently serious: the prospect disclosed an anxiety disorder and a chronic fight-or-flight pattern, and the rep then pre-framed the buying decision as a fight-or-flight moment and asked him in advance whether he would push through the feeling — disarming the money objection before it could be raised, using the prospect's own disclosed condition. The money concern was then raised anyway, tied to an unstable job, and was never explored before $9,000 was taken. The recorder was again switched off at the payment step.

quality.notes: Sustained inversion, worst in the closing third where the labels effectively swap for long runs — 'Do you want me to show you how we can help you? Definitely.' at 00:20:54 and 'Ready to rock and roll?' at 00:32:37 are both labelled Andrew but are the rep, while 'Yep, I am' and 'Let's do it' are labelled Farooq Bey but are the prospect. Similarly 'Congrats, by the way, you're getting married soon' at 00:05:08 is labelled correctly but the surrounding turns are not. One garbled artefact at 00:15:00 renders 'step into that version of yourself' as 'step into that version of Fathom'. Roles resolved from content throughout; no line-level attribution should be trusted.
